title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Incident reporting
decisions.scenario: A patient experiences a fall in the room but does not appear injured and denies pain.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Restraint ethics
decisions.scenario: A confused patient becomes increasingly restless and attempts to leave the unit. Staff suggest restraints as a quick solution.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Privacy during care
decisions.scenario: While providing bedside care, the patient’s curtains remain open, and other patients and visitors can see into the area.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Provide privacy and cover the patient.

decisions.title: Resource allocation
decisions.scenario: During a busy shift, limited resources require decisions about which patients receive immediate attention first.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Conflict of interest
decisions.scenario: A nurse promotes a healthcare product to patients while receiving personal benefits from the product supplier.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Avoid the conflict and disclose appropriately.

decisions.title: Student supervision
decisions.scenario: A student nurse performs a clinical skill incorrectly while under your supervision, and the patient’s safety could be affected.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelWhy: Patient safety and education are priorities.

decisions.title: Legal documentation request
decisions.scenario: A legal representative contacts the unit requesting access to a patient’s medical records without going through formal hospital channels.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Professional accountability
decisions.scenario: You make a clinical judgment error that affects patient care outcomes. The mistake is recognised after the situation has been stabilised.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Acknowledge and learn from the error.
